### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **9** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, touching **105** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **70** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c96d3211551fd414721a4ca4f81119036a95fe47` — the merge of head `b94d1ac68d151d99ad908992ad25f65bf2413a6d` into base `23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c96d3211551fd414721a4ca4f81119036a95fe47 && git checkout c96d3211551fd414721a4ca4f81119036a95fe47
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006 b94d1ac68d151d99ad908992ad25f65bf2413a6d && git checkout -B drift-repro 23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006 && git merge --no-ff b94d1ac68d151d99ad908992ad25f65bf2413a6d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 23cf11a4b9f3fa8c7291b5d7a308c5d14793b006` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The head moved from `1340933c` to `ee5587b4` during this review (one docs-only commit, read in full). Merge-tree against today's `origin/main` `022b4e7e`: clean.

### ① Lookup threading — behaviour unchanged

- **The lookup is inert by construction.** `appOf(packageId, installed)` is `void installed; return packageId;` (`customization-pair-lookup.ts` 103–106); `pairOf` and `isPairOf` only forward `installed` to it (113–127). So every `pairOf(x, L)` ≡ `customizationPackageId(x)` and every `isPairOf(p, x, L)` ≡ `isCustomizationPairOf(p, x)` for every lookup `L`, refusal reasons included (`base_id_missing`, `base_is_customization_package`, `base_id_invalid` all still come from the spec helper). Nit 4 of PR 1 holds: `pairOf('x.custom', L)` is still refused. The unit table pins exactly this for six shapes × two lookups (nothing installed; every row installed with the HotCRM module declaring its App), plus the refusal rows under both lookups (`customization-pair-lookup.test.ts` 61–129). TRUE.
- **`installedManifestsOf` cannot throw on a lookup that answers nothing** (`customization-pair-lookup.ts` 86–92: no registry / no `getPackage` → `NOTHING_INSTALLED`; a non-object manifest → `undefined`), pinned by the six `it.each` sources (test 76–87). `installedManifestsOfEngine(engine)` is the same over `engine?.registry` (`installed-manifests.ts` 19–22).
- **Every site moved only its argument list.** I read all 23 `pairOf` / `isPairOf` hunks and the `isServedOverrideRowOf` callers: discovery 409, environment-rows 121–147 and 295–304, lock-state 149–173, layered 403–417 (sort ranks unchanged), list reads 86 / 200 / 274 / 363 / 534 / 569 / 678 / 894, overlay-merge 96–99 and 327–340, package-bindings 273–282, packaged-base-refusal 165–176 / 195–235 / 430 / 690–700 / 1099–1100 / 1290–1292, packageless-migration 381–397 / 461 / 478 / 616 / 679 / 801, registry-hydration 527, served-overrides 97–118, write-gates 641–659, served-override 88–96, stored-flow-slot 89–97, class-head 186–192, diff-delete-load 428–431 / 1167–1171. Branches, status codes, sentences and sort order are byte-identical around each call. TRUE.
- **The type seam is sound.** `ServedOverlayAddress` (overlay-merge 114–146) and `mergePackageAwareOverlay`'s `options` (282–299) are discriminated unions: `servedOverride` without `installed` does not compile, so no serving read can lose its pair silently; the two callers that pass `{ packageId }` alone (overlay-merge 167, the view-container package order) passed no `servedOverride` on `main` either. `OverrideWriteClosure.installed` is required (packaged-base-refusal 846–852), so the compiler names every caller — which is why `cli` and `cloud-connection` are in the diff.
- **Sites whose answer could move — each checked, none moves.** `cli` offline (`override-declarations.ts` 114–116): the lookup is `byId.get(id)?.manifest` over the artifact's own walked manifests, no registry, so an offline validate reads the same artifact it already read. `cloud-connection` install-local (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` 3823–3829): delivered manifest first, else `installedManifestsOf(registry)`; the registry was already read for `dependenciesOf` on `main`. `objectql` plugin (`plugin.ts` 3842–3851): `installedManifestsOf(this.ql.registry)`, the registry it already held; built once per call, not per row. Flow precedence (`flow-precedence.ts` 143–151, 184–191, 261–263, 345–348, 392): the lookup is a fourth required parameter; `undeclaredRemedy`'s sentence is unchanged. Served-override row readers: all 17 non-test callers pass `installedManifestsOfEngine(host.engine)` or the registry they hold. Write gate (`overrideWriteVerdict` 1290–1292; `judgeOverrideWrite` 1099–1100): same `pairOf` / `isPairOf` pair as before. Runtime `customizeInPairRemedy` (`packages.ts` 676–681) and `readPackageCustomizations` (3992–3993) — the two deferred PR 1 sites — now go through `pairOf`; identity, so the remedy sentence and the extensions read are unchanged. Lint 108: `isCustomizationPackage(manifest.id)` replaces the `base_is_customization_package` parse — the one edge the body names (`a.custom.custom`, bare `.custom`) is a `base_id_invalid` input that the old parse also did not skip-by-reason, so the advisory's outcome on real manifests is the same.
- **Registries newly held; ordering and boot.** No site holds a registry it could not reach before. The protocol facets gain `engine` on their host `Pick`s and `protocol.ts` hands it over as a lazy getter (`get engine() { return readEngine(); }`, six sites 3827–7263): read at call time, never at construction, so no boot-order change. The one genuinely new service read is `service-automation/plugin.ts` 594–600 `objectqlRegistryOf(ctx)`: `ctx.getService('objectql')` inside `try { } catch { return undefined; }`, called at the boot pull (5245) beside the loader set. An absent or not-yet-registered objectql answers "nothing installed" → identity → the same precedence. It introduces no await and no dependency ordering, only an optional read, the same shape as the plugin's `flowHistoryReader` read. `service-datasource` (`plugin.ts` 223–229) refactors its existing `safeGetService('objectql')` read into `objectqlRegistry()`; no new read. `registry.ts` 7337 passes `installedManifestsOf(this)`. So: no new boot read, no ordering change, no registry a caller did not already own. TRUE.

### ② The kernel verdict

- **What "kernel base" is.** `kernelPackageScopeOf(row)` (`protocol-customization-package.ts` 162–165) = the installed manifest's `scope` ∈ `READ_ONLY_PACKAGE_SCOPES` = `['system', 'cloud']` (`package-writability.ts` 38). It is a manifest-scope test, not a namespace test: `sys` is not read, and a `project`-scoped package of namespace `sys` would not be kernel. Exported as `kernelPackageScope(engine, id)` (170–174) for the clone doors. Every `scope: 'system'` declaration under `packages/**` non-test (35 sites) is a platform-delivered package: the plugins (`plugin-auth`, `plugin-security`, `organizations`, …), the services, `platform-objects`, the platform apps (`apps/account`, `apps/setup`, `apps/studio`), the UI contributions of `cloud-connection` / `mcp`. HotCRM declares no `scope` (its five manifests), so it is not kernel.
- **Misclassification.** The manifest schema admits `scope: 'system' | 'cloud'` on any manifest (`manifest.zod.ts` 636, default `project`), and no install path stamps, strips or refuses it (grepped `registry.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, runtime `packages.ts`: the scope is read as posture, never written). So a vendor App that mis-declares `scope: 'system'` would be read as kernel and get no pair. That is a pre-existing meaning of the scope — `isWritablePackage` 80 and `isDisableableAppModule` (`packages.ts` 759) already treat it as "the platform's", and the dev's own fixtures had modelled "an installed app" as `scope: 'system'` and were moved to `code` (`packages-ensure-customization.test.ts` 63–69, `automation-flow-clone-custom-package.test.ts` 68–73). The predicate is the right one for this version; the vendor's remedy (drop the scope) belongs in the changeset's "who moves" (nit 4).
- **409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.** A standard ledger member (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts` 2001 `shadows: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`; `error-code-ledger.test.ts` 71), already the door's code for a writable base, no namespace, a bad pair namespace, a non-SemVer version and a malformed existing pair (`customizationPairEnsureRefusal` 363–406; `expectRefusal(r, 409, 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', …)` on each in the runtime test). No new ledger row, no `packages/spec` edit (the file list carries none). The message (353–358): "Package '<id>' is a kernel package (scope '<scope>'): kernel objects are not customizable in this version, so '<id>' has no paired customization package and '<id>.custom' is not ensured. A pair an earlier version created stays installed, and the overrides in it stay served (ADR-0146 D3)." Readable, names the base, the scope and the pair id, says "in this version" and nothing about which objects may open later — neutral about the whitelist. TRUE. `check:error-status-conformance` exit 0 in the dev's gate list.
- **Nothing is created.** The verdict is the second judgement in `customizationPairEnsureRefusal` (after the 404 for an uninstalled base, 341–359) and `ensurePairOnce` throws whatever that function answers before reading the version or calling `installPackage` (416–448). `ensureCustomizationPackage` itself only parses, derives the pair id and takes the in-flight slot before `ensurePairOnce` (280–330); nothing is written on the refused path. The `leavesNothing` harness pins it for `system` and `cloud` plus `getPackage('<id>.custom') === undefined` (runtime test 254–266).
- **Legacy kernel pairs.** The door's `existing` branch is below the kernel check, so a legacy `<kernel>.custom` is neither adopted nor rewritten: the refusal says it stays (354–357) and the pin compares the registry row before/after (`structuredClone`, runtime test 268–280) and reads it 200. Served: the objectql pin installs the pair under a `scope: 'system'` base, saves a declared override, gets 409 on ensure, then reads the override on the by-name, package-scoped, layered and list reads (`protocol-custom-override-effective-read.test.ts` 475–493). Writable: the write gate is `judgeOverrideWrite` over `pairOf` / `isPairOf` — identity, no ensure-door read anywhere in `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` 1060–1110 — and the same pin lands a second save into the pair (494–496). TRUE.
- **The two closes.** `overlayPairFixOf` (packaged-base-refusal 427–445) answers `null` when `customizationPairEnsureRefusal` answers a refusal, and the package-less close and the named-base close then leave the save open — the existing family for every base the door refuses (the docblock at 336–347 says so). For a kernel item that means: package-less save onto a kernel-shipped overlay-type item, `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` naming the pair on `main` → admitted now; a save naming the kernel package → admitted (effective-read test 498–515, with an App control that still gets 403). This is a **widening**, and it is in the body's table but not in the Clause-② line (should-fix 1). Its governing text is PR #31027's Q10 ("its package-less write stays open until the kernel whitelist admits the item into the platform pair", *decided where the rulings were silent*), which is unmerged; ruling 6691217245 itself says every kernel object is served as not customizable and says nothing about reopening the package-less write D11 closed. Contract question for the seat (should-fix 2), not a code defect: the code follows the ensure-door family as designed.
- **Narrowing declaration.** Clause-② `yes (narrowing)` at line start in both carriers, one each; `Metadata-protocol: none` (right: no authorable key, value or meaning moves; the ensure response schema is untouched). Changeset: patch on the nine packages whose dist changes; `**BREAKING** for a caller that ensures the customization pair of a kernel package … and for a TypeScript importer of the pair helpers`; who moves and the one-line remedy ("drops that call …; passes `installedManifestsOf(engine.registry)`, or `installedManifestsOf(undefined)`") present; `adr-0087: not-required` comment reasoned. The `!` title + patch bumps pass `check-changeset-no-major` (exit 0 in the gate list) and `Check Changeset` is green on both heads. The Clause-② line names the ensure door, the clone landing and the retyped helpers; it omits the reopened closes (widening) and the flow clone's new 409 (a second narrowing row in the table) — one sentence (should-fix 1).
- **Flow clone of a kernel-shipped flow.** `resolveCloneTarget` (`automation.ts` 2608–2618) relays the ensure door's thrown 409 through `deps.errorFromThrown`, and `registerAndSaveFlow` 2463–2474 calls `restoreFlowRegistration` on a refused landing, so the engine registration made before `land()` is undone and nothing is created. Correct, and in the table; no pin covers that row (should-fix 4).

### ③ The clone collision (option A)

- **Is the "new notice code" a published spec key?** No. `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_NOTICE_CODES` lives in `packages/runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts` 186–191 and nowhere under `packages/spec/**` on `main` or on the head (`git grep` of all four codes: runtime, dogfood, the Console's reader `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/permission-set-clone.ts` 90–94 and two UI tests, CHANGELOGs). The clone response's `noticeCode` is an untyped string the Console switches on, with a documented fallback to the served `notice` for an unknown code (the UI test at `StudioDesignSurface.accessNewSimilar-28573.test.tsx` 360 pins `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_SOMEWHERE_NEWER` → sentence as sent). So the new value `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_ENVIRONMENT_WIDE_KERNEL_SOURCE` is a new runtime value on an existing untyped field, not a new ledger row and not a `packages/spec` edit; no spec fence is crossed. It is nonetheless a new value a client may switch on — the body declares it in the Clause-② line, the changeset and now `permission-sets.mdx` 456–460, and the dev's out-of-scope note hands the zh sentence to the ui lane. Flagged here as the seat asked; nothing to stop the PR.
- **Is landing environment-wide safe?** The copy takes a new machine name: `taken || target.name === source.name` → `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_NAME_TAKEN_STATUS` after a catalog resolve of the target name (`permission-set-clone.ts` 497–525), and the save is create-only, with `METADATA_CONFLICT` re-answered as name-taken (585–595). `permission_set` is not an overridable type (`served-override.test.ts` 66: `isServedOverrideRowOf` is `false` for it), so an environment-wide row cannot be read as an override of anything, and a same-name shadow is refused by the name check. The grants are the source's, judged as inherited (`inheritedGrantObjects`, 576–583), unchanged from the environment-authored landing. What changes for the operator is only where the copy lives (no package, so it does not travel with one) — the notice says so and names `package` as the way to keep it in a package (210–215). The kernel item itself is untouched. A named `package` still goes through `newSimilarTargetRefusal` (544–550). No shadow, no override, nothing unintended.
- **Option B instead.** `resolveDefaultCloneLanding` 319–323 is the whole switch: replace the `return { packageId: null, created: false, kernelSource }` with a thrown refusal (409, naming `package=<a writable package of yours>`), drop `kernelSource` from `PermissionSetCloneLanding` (168–172), the fourth code and its sentence (186–215), the unit pin (`permission-set-clone.test.ts` 247–261) and the four-code table rows (369–375 → three), re-point the dogfood pin (`permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts` 231–248) to the refusal, and revert the `permission-sets.mdx` sentence. About 60 lines across four files plus the docs line; the kernel verdict and the lookup threading are untouched. Option C would reopen the ensure door for a clone source, against the ruling, and would be a larger change in the door. The maintainer's card is open; A is implemented and reversible.

### ④ Tests, ablations, dogfood, gates (the dev's readings; `Local-runs: none`)

- Lookup: the identity pinned under two lookups × six shapes + refusals (metadata-core 962 green). Kernel verdict: `system` and `cloud` 409 with nothing created, legacy pair unchanged and readable (runtime 8851 green); legacy override served on four reads and a further save lands; the two closes reopen for a kernel item with an App control (objectql 11211 green). Clone: unit pin (no ensure, `packageId` absent on the save, the code and the sentence), the four-code distinctness table, the dogfood pin re-pointed (`package: null`, the code, `GET /packages/<kernel>.custom` 404). Adapted suites: 22489 metadata-protocol, 8288 lint, 1279 datasource, 3431 automation, 931 cloud-connection, 7415 cli — all pass with the lookup passed; no test skipped, quarantined or deleted.
- Ablations (server-lane negative-pin rule): kernel check disabled (dist preflight confirmed) → 3 runtime + 2 objectql pins red; clone landing disabled → its unit pin red; both restored, blob == HEAD, tree clean. The lookup threading has no ablation by design (nothing to red; the table pins both lookups equal). Honest shape.
- Dogfood battery on `021a8a3d` (the two later commits are test warm-imports and docs): first run 1 failed — the very pin that found the collision — final run exit 0, 428 files, 3562 tests. The body says so and names the commit.
- Gates: `dispatch-gates --commands` 75 families, `--ran` 75/75, 0 NOT-MEASURED; three first-pass non-zeros fixed and re-run to 0 (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` after fetching the pinned fixture commit; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` after a full build; `check:test-source-alias` with the four warm imports that are the `1340933c` commit). eslint `--no-inline-config` exit 0 on every changed `.ts`.

### ⑤ Commits and body
